parties:
Quazi Nasibul Hasan (Sunnu)  -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Bank and others  -------- Respondents.
full_judgment: "The primary liability for repayment lies upon the borrower and upon his failure to pay the same, the guarantor is liable to pay it. It may well be the case that an influential person of high standing guarantees the repayment of a loan obtained by his employee or some other poor person to whom the bank is reluctant to provide credit. If the borrower in such cases defaults the guarantor is no doubt liable to repay the loan, but it would be unfair to an innocent guarantor if his name is included in the CIB list and all banking transaction suddenly stopped. In our opinion, that could not have been the intention of the legislature. In such case no one will come forward to guarantee loan taken by a person of lesser means. In course of default if a case is filed under the Artha Rin Ain for recovery of loan amount the guarantor can be joined as a party in the suit for recovery of loan money and decree may be passed against both the borrower and the guarantor but, even according to the Artha Rin Ain, the decree can be executed against the guarantor only if it remains unsatisfied by proceedings against the principal borrower. This is to give protection to the guarantor. Similarly, if a person stands guarantee for a loan disbursed to a borrower and if the borrower fails to repay the loan within the stipulated period or even to keep up with the installments, the borrower's name may be included in the CIB list but not that of the guarantor. "
